local.title: High Falls to light orange for domestic violence awareness
local.summary: The High Falls in downtown will light up orange on Wednesday as part of a Zonta Club of Rochester initiative to raise awareness of domestic violence against women and girls.
local.body:
The High Falls in downtown will light up orange on Wednesday as part of a Zonta Club of Rochester initiative to raise awareness of domestic violence against women and girls.

"There isn't always closure for a lot of women, and so by calling attention to this, we're hoping that people will just be more aware, and that women who perhaps are victims will feel more empowered to get out of the situation that they are in," says Bonnie Abrams, a past president and current advocacy co-chair at Zonta Club.

A 2025 report shows domestic violence incidents in the City of Rochester are 2.4 times higher than the statewide rates, and the Monroe County rates are nearly double the state numbers, according to the Willow Domestic Violence Center.

"Though domestic violence occurs on all social strata, you know, but I think that unfortunately there are more incidents because of people feeling powerless, and I think that that's perhaps one of the reasons that the statistics are higher here in Rochester, and that's another reason why we want to call attention to this issue," she explained.

Abrams says the word "Zonta" comes from the Lakota word meaning "honest" or "trustworthy". She says she wants everyone to know there are trusted people willing to help.

The Rochester branch is part of a national network that first started in Buffalo. They issue grants and other support to organizations that further its mission to improve the lives of women and girls.

The falls lighting will kick off the club's 16 Days of Activism that runs through Human Rights Day on December 10th.

The event starts at Genesee Brew House at 5 p.m. Participants will walk over for the falls lighting and a proclamation reading from Mayor Malik Evans' office. A local survivor of domestic violence will serve as speaker.

entertainment.title: Steven Hack, Original ‘Cats’ Castmember and Busy Onscreen Character Actor, Dies at 68
entertainment.summary: His credits ranged from ‘Jake and the Fatman’ and ‘Seinfeld’ to ‘Pam & Tommy’ and ‘Amsterdam.’
entertainment.body:
Steven Hack, the theater veteran who spent five years on Broadway as an original castmember in Cats , then appeared as a character actor in dozens of films and TV shows, has died. He was 68.

Hack died Thursday at home following what was described as “a sudden and unexpected cardiac event,” the Interact Theatre Company announced . He was a founding member of the North Hollywood-based group that launched in 1989.

“Steven was a gifted and versatile performer, a superb graphic artist and a cherished member of our artistic family,” ITC directors Barry Heins and Walter Ware said in a statement. “His creativity and talent helped shape Interact in its earliest years, and his artistry, humor, warmth and generous spirit enriched everything he touched.” Related Stories Lifestyle The Pulitzer-Winning Play 'Purpose' Finally Came to Los Angeles. But That Doesn't Mean It's Gone Hollywood. Lifestyle 'The Comedy About Spies' to Open on Broadway This Spring

Born in St. Louis on April 20, 1958, Hack studied at CalArts and The American Academy of Dramatic Arts in Los Angeles. In 1978, he was a background dancer in the film version of Grease and appeared in the off-Broadway musical The Coolest Cat in Town .

Hack was there when Andrew Lloyd Webber’s Cats opened at the Winter Garden Theatre on Oct. 7, 1982, and he portrayed several characters, including Coricopat, Mungojerrie, Carbucketty, Tumblebrutus and Pouncival, over the next five years.

He toured with Michael Bennett’s A Chorus Line for nearly two years and then joined the Broadway production at the Shubert Theatre for one show only — its record-breaking 3,389th Great White Way performance on Sept. 29, 1983. (He did Cats that night, too.)

Hack started showing up on television in the 1990s on shows including The Trials of Rosie O’Neill , Jake and the Fatman , Matlock , Dr. Quinn, Medicine Woman , Married … With Children , Seinfeld , Mad About You and Caroline in the City .

More recently, he found work in the series American Horror Story , Ratched , Perry Mason and Not Dead Yet , in the miniseries Pam & Tommy and Angelyne and in the films Thor: The Dark World (2013), Fantastic Four (2015), The Happytime Murders (2018) and Amsterdam (2022).

entertainment.title: The Pulitzer-Winning Play ‘Purpose’ Finally Came to Los Angeles. But That Doesn’t Mean It’s Gone Hollywood.
entertainment.summary: Branden Jacobs-Jenkins reunites the entire company, including Kara Young and director Phylicia Rashad, for a sold-out run at the Geffen Playhouse.
entertainment.body:
Branden Jacobs-Jenkins is, famously, a tinkerer. His plays go through long, thoughtful development processes. He first wrote Appropriate a decade before it became the 2024 Tony Award-winning play starring Sarah Paulson. His next work, Purpose , went through a nuanced workshop with the actors before it premiered at the Steppenwolf Theatre in Chicago; the company finalized the ending one day before the first performance. “They were walking on stage with pages in hand, that’s how fresh it was,” says Jacobs-Jenkins. “But they say the great writers all rewrite — Arthur Miller was rewriting his plays at the end of his life. Shakespeare obviously was rewriting King Lear over and over again.” Related Stories Lifestyle 'The Comedy About Spies' to Open on Broadway This Spring Lifestyle 'Birthright,' About Differing Attitudes on Israel, Set For Broadway

Director Phylicia Rashad is quick to point out that she sees Jacobs-Jenkins’ process as a gift, noting how rare it is for a company to have success access to the playwright during rehearsals. “I’ve only had this experience once before, with August Wilson and Gem of the Ocean ,” she says. “The first production I did was here in Los Angeles at the Mark Taper forum, and then it went to the Huntington in Boston and eventually to Broadway — he continued to refine that play until we opened on Broadway, and I loved it.” Plus, she adds of Jacobs-Jenkins, “You cannot tell a playwright, this genius, ‘You have got to have this by three o’clock tomorrow.’ That doesn’t work.”

Purpose eventually transferred to Broadway, where it won best play and best performance by an actress in a featured role (for Kara Young ), as well as the 2025 Pulitzer Prize for drama. But Jacobs-Jenkins says that despite the accolades he still hopes to polish it until the bitter end. “Every time I hear the play I think: I want to change this or that,” he laughs.

The storied stage play, which centers on a politically dynastic Black family (not entirely unlike that of the Reverend Jesse Jackson) during a dinner welcoming their eldest home from his white collar crime prison stint, is now in the midst of a revival at Los Angeles’ Geffen Playhouse . The entire Broadway cast, along with Rashad, reunited for the L.A. run, an occasion that proved both historic and also tempting for a playwright who loves the chance to revisit his work. “I actually felt a lot of pressure to leave it alone, because so many people want to see the Broadway production,” he says. “So I can’t just be out here messing with the thing. I don’t want to rock the boat.”

entertainment.title: Mary J. Blige Ruling, Cher Sonny Bono Lawsuit, Julio Iglesias Case & More Top Music Law News
entertainment.summary: In this week's Legal Beat newsletter, a big ruling on "Real Love," Cher's battle with Sonny's widow, an abuse probe for Julio Iglesias and much more.
entertainment.body:
THE BIG STORY: Mary J. Blige won a court ruling this week that was more than 50 years in the making —and one that offers a history lesson on both hip-hop and music law.

When Blige released her song “Real Love” in 1992, it featured elements of “Impeach the President” by The Honey Drippers — a 1973 protest funk song that was widely sampled in the early days of rap and has made appearances in tracks by Run-DMC , Dr. Dre , LL Cool J and, more recently, Doja Cat . “Impeach” was so ubiquitous that Blige seems to have used it indirectly, via a direct sample of a different 1987 hip-hop track that had sampled it.

Decades later, in 2024, a label called Tuff City Records, which owns the famous sample, took UMG to court over it. And the lawsuit revealed that a strange situation had played out behind the scenes: Apparently, UMG’s recorded music unit quickly settled and agreed to pay for the sample, but its publishing unit refused to do so, choosing instead to fight it out in court over whether it also had to pay.

Case in point: Despite the use of the sample of the recording, a judge sided with UMG last year on the composition, dismissing Tuff City’s case on the grounds that “the songs do not sound the same.” And in a new ruling this week , a federal appeals court affirmed that decision, ruling that Blige’s song was simply not similar enough to The Honey Drippers’ to count as infringement of the underlying music.

What about that history lesson? Well, back in 1991, Tuff City filed another case over “Impeach the President,” that time suing Sony Music for allegedly featuring it on two LL Cool J tracks. At the time, uncleared sampling was widely accepted in hip-hop, but a 1992 New York Times article warned that Tuff City’s lawsuit could change all that.

That abundance of caution has often led to also paying for the underlying composition to the same track — precisely what UMG refused to do here. Will the “Real Love” ruling embolden other artists and labels to do the same?

— A Spanish court launched an investigation into singer Julio Iglesias over accusations that he sexually and physically abused two female employees at his Caribbean residences.

— Members of the Americana band The Mavericks said they were “saddened” by a lawsuit filed by the widow of late frontman Raul Malo seeking to ban them from using the band’s name.

entertainment.title: See Kristen Stewart’s Out of This World Transformation into Sally Ride
entertainment.summary: Where the hell has Kristen Stewart been, loca? Well, in short, outer space. For the Twilight actress’ latest role as groundbreaking NASA astronaut Sally Ride—a.k.a. the first American woman to...
entertainment.body:
Well, in short, outer space. For the Twilight actress ’ latest role as groundbreaking NASA astronaut Sally Ride —a.k.a. the first American woman to fly in space—in The Challenger, she fully changed up her look, rocking a look straight out of the ‘80s.

Stewart donned a brunette bob on the Georgia set of the Prime Video limited series Nov. 24, completing her look with a 1980s style shirt—tied with a bow at the collar—and a dark pair of bottoms. The 36-year-old kept warm on set with a fluffy zip-up sweater as she sipped on a Diet Coke between takes.

The role marks the Oscar nominee’s first regular TV role, with her also serving as a producer on the series alongside wife Dylan Meyers through their production company Nevermind Pictures.

And for Stewart, she couldn’t believe she had the chance to bring Ride’s story to life.

“I’m shaking in boots, but I get to play Sally Ride,” she shared with Collider in December. “The story is incredible and the team is just so inspired and trustworthy and I think I'm in the safest hands.”

The limited series is inspired by Meredith E. Bagby ’s 2023 book The New Guys , which chronicled the story of Ride and her fellow astronauts who all broke barriers as NASA’s 1978 astronaut class.

In addition to being the first American woman—and third woman—to fly in space in 1983 , Ride also served on the committees that investigated the explosions of the Space Shuttle Challenger in 1986 and the Space Shuttle Columbia in 2003, making her the only person to participate in both.

While she was married to fellow astronaut Steven Hawley from 1982 to 1987, Ride was in a long term relationship with women’s tennis star Tam O’Shaughnessy from 1985 until her death in 2012 from pancreatic cancer at the age of 61. However, Ride hid the fact that she was part of the LGBTQ community during her lifetime, with the news only coming out when O’Shaughnessy was noted to have been her partner of 27 years in her obituary .

entertainment.title: 100 Years of Music at Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade, For ‘An Audience Aged 1 to 100’
entertainment.summary: “It’s your Thanksgiving Day playlist, it’s your annual yearbook,” Will Coss of Macy’s Studios tells Billboard of booking artists over a century of parades.
entertainment.body:
No holiday tradition sums up America quite like the Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade.

For more than a century now, the annual extravaganza has wound its way from Manhattan’s Upper West Side through Midtown Manhattan and across Herald Square to the famous star outside the historic Macy’s flagship store on 34th Street.

Filled with giant balloons, colorful floats, clowns, musical performances, squads of cheerleaders and marching bands, the parade has become nothing short of a holiday institution. In fact, the event has taken place every year since 1924, with the exception of just two years when it was put on pause during World War II.

As it’s grown, the parade has also reached far beyond the streets of New York City, with NBC broadcasting all the fun, music and magic live coast to coast since the late 1950s. In any given household, odds are, the parade will be on the television come Thanksgiving morning, providing a cozy and familiar tradition as turkeys are basted, potatoes are mashed and finishing touches are put on each pie.

Macy’s annual parade has become an integral, often cherished part of the day, as families, friends and loved ones gather around kitchen tables. For many parade lovers, the march through Manhattan heralds the official start of the holiday season, thanks to Tom Turkey’s ever-trusty appearance at the head of the parade and Santa’s arrival in his giant sleigh signaling the grand finale.

Remarkably, this year’s holiday marks the 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade, which is set to air live on NBC, Peacock and Telemundo on Thursday morning (Nov. 26) from 8:30 a.m. to noon ET.

entertainment.title: Netflix Buys Radford Studio Lot for $380 Million
entertainment.summary: The purchase gives the entertainment giant ownership of a major Los Angeles production campus.
entertainment.body:
Netflix is buying Radford Studio Center for $380 million, taking ownership of one of Hollywood’s most storied production lots as the entertainment giant expands its physical footprint in Los Angeles.

The deal, which is expected to close on Tuesday, follows an auction during which the property’s lender took back the property after Hackman Capital Partners defaulted on its mortgage amid historically low production levels in the region. Netflix reached an agreement with the Goldman Sachs-led lender to acquire the lot.

The $380 million price point is roughly 20 percent of the $1.85 billion Hackman paid for Radford in 2021, a massive repricing of a legacy Hollywood lot and indicative of the flight of filming away from Los Angeles and California. Related Stories Business Bela Bajaria Calls Time at Netflix a "Fun Chapter" as She Teases Rest and "Conversations" in First Remarks on Exit Movies Sadie Sandler to Star in Netflix Horror Movie 'Malibu' From Vertigo, Happy Madison (Exclusive)

After it took over the property, Goldman handled the foreclosure to facilitate a sale. As part of the deal, Netflix paid the so-called mansion tax, which imposes a 5.5 percent levy for properties valued above $10.9 million, says a person familiar with the sale.

As part of the deal, Netflix has pacted with Louis Dargenzio’s rising studio services firm Zello, contracting with its entertainment advisory division ZVantage to manage the transition as well as partnering with Dargenzio’s production equipment provider Cinelease to provide services. (Cinelease is a rival to Quixote, which is owned by the studio services giant Hudson Pacific that Netflix currently leases from at Sunset Studios.)

The purchase will shake up Netflix’s production pipeline in L.A. For years, it’s been the anchor tenant at Sunset Studios while also filming at Raleigh Studios. With the 55-acre shooting campus, the company could consolidate production scattered across the region while cutting costs associated with renting.

In a memo to staff, Netflix said that it purchased Radford to “strengthen our investment in Los Angeles and California.”

“This city is home to us,” it said. “We’re excited to keep investing here and finding more ways to entertain the world, while supporting the writers, builders, electricians, drivers, designers, and talent who make L.A., California, and the entertainment industry so special.”

entertainment.title: Nick Carter Ordered to Stand Trial on Sexual Assault Claims From Dream Singer Melissa Schuman
entertainment.summary: The Backstreet Boys member denies assaulting Schuman or any of the other women who've accused him of sexual misconduct.
entertainment.body:
A judge has decided to hold a trial in the sexual assault lawsuit brought against Backstreet Boys member Nick Carter by Melissa Schuman, a former member of the teen-pop group Dream .

A Monday (Nov. 23) court ruling, obtained by Billboard , says there “is a triable issue of material fact” as to whether Carter forced Schuman to have sex when they were co-starring in the teen horror movie The Hollow in 2003. A trial is set for May 2027 in Santa Monica, Calif.

Schuman sued Carter in 2023 under California’s Sexual Abuse and Cover-Up Accountability Act, a state law that temporarily lifted the statute of limitations for otherwise-expired sex assault claims. Under that law, claims only qualified for revival if there was an allegation that some business entity had conspired to “cover up” a prior sexual assault by the same perpetrator.

Carter vehemently denies Schuman’s sexual battery claim and has countersued her, as well as various other sexual assault accusers, for defamation. His lawyers argued that Schuman’s case had a fatal defect: she failed to allege the right kind of cover-up, meaning it was not eligible for California’s 2023 claim revival window.

However, California passed another law last year, called the Justice for Survivors of Sexual Assault Act, that opened another two-year window for sexual assault claims with looser cover-up requirements. Judge Lisa K. Sepe-Wiesenfeld ruled Monday that this second law can be successfully used to revive Schuman’s claims.

“The individual claim against defendant Carter for sexual battery is proper irrespective of the existence of a cover up,” wrote the judge. “Defendants cannot prevail on summary adjudication merely by attacking the cover-up allegations.”

The question at this stage, then, is merely whether there’s enough conflicting evidence in the case to go to a jury. Judge Sepe-Wiesenfeld believes the answer is yes, since Schuman has said that Carter assaulted her, while the singer said it never happened.

“There is a conflict in the evidence presented as to whether a sexual assault of Plaintiff occurred,” wrote the judge.

entertainment.title: The Rings Of Power: How The Númenóreans Helped Save Middle-Earth, Explained
entertainment.summary: In one of the most recent episodes of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power, the history of the Númenóreans is brought up. Here's what that's referring to.
entertainment.body:
Ben Rothstein/Prime Add TVLine on Google: Preferred Source Google Discover Contains spoilers for "The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power" Season 3, Episode 5 — "The Lady of Lórien"

Early in "The Rings of Power" Season 3, Episode 5 , Elros tells his brother Elrond (both played by Robert Aramayo) that he's chosen a mortal life and the path of death, which Tolkien called the Gift of Men . The grief-stricken Elrond brings up that trading immortality for a crown, glory, and titles isn't worth it, but Elros sees it as a great honor to help his human friends. In the midst of the argument about the fallibility of Men, Elrond says, "Men fall, Elros, so easily." Elros replies, "Yes, but the Men of Númenor will be different. They helped save Middle-earth. Perhaps one day they will do so again."

The line is referencing specific events, both before and after "The Rings of Power" story is set. Men's future role in helping save Middle-earth is seen throughout Tolkien's writings, most famously in "The Lord of the Rings." But what is Elros talking about when he says Men saved Middle-earth in the past?

"The Rings of Power" is set in the Second Age, thousands of years before "The Lord of the Rings." The first King of Númenor's line references a part Men play even earlier than that, when some of them helped take down the original Dark Lord Morgoth at the end of the First Age of Middle-earth.

Prime Video Men enter Tolkien's story at the beginning of the First Age when Morgoth is the poster child of evil across Arda (Tolkien's name for the world). As they enter Arda, most Men fall under Morgoth's influence. That's how you get nations like Rhûn in the East of Middle-earth (which we continued to see quite a bit of through the eyes of Gandalf in "The Rings of Power" Season 3, Episode 3 ).

The majority of the human race are ensnared by evil, but some resist the Darkness. "The Silmarillion" explains, "There were some that turned from evil and left the lands of their kindred, and wandered ever westward; for they had heard a rumour that in the West there was a light which the Shadow could not dim." These humans are chased relentlessly by Morgoth, but they join forces with the Elves (also called the Eldar) to resist their enemy. The book adds, "The Edain these were named in the Sindarin tongue; and they became friends and allies of the Eldar, and did deeds of great valour in the war against Morgoth."

entertainment.title: Ella Langley’s ‘Choosin’ Texas’ Ties Hot Country Songs Record With 50 Weeks at No. 1
entertainment.summary: The hit matches Bebe Rexha and Florida Georgia Line’s “Meant To Be.”
entertainment.body:
Ella Langley ’s “Choosin’ Texas” logs a 50th week atop Billboard ’s Hot Country Songs chart (dated Nov. 28), matching the all-time record set by Bebe Rexha and Florida Georgia Line ’s “Meant To Be” in 2017-18.

“Choosin’ Texas” totaled 16.9 million official streams, 45.5 million in airplay audience and 6,000 sales in the United States Nov. 13-19, according to Luminate.

The song also extends its Billboard Hot 100 record to 29 weeks at No. 1.

Here’s a rundown of the five longest-leading Hot Country Songs hits (since the list became the genre’s singular songs chart in October 1958):

“Meant To Be” debuted atop Hot Country Songs in December 2017 and held the summit for 50 consecutive weeks. “Choosin’ Texas” reached No. 1 in its sixth week, in February, and led for 28 frames before Taylor Swift’s “I Knew It, I Knew You” interrupted its reign for two weeks in June. Langley reclaimed the summit on the July 4 chart and has remained there for 22 more weeks in a row.

The shared milestone also links two distinct moments in country’s crossover history. “Meant To Be” emerged during a sonically experimental boom, pairing pop star Rexha with FGL, a country cornerstone act in the 2010s, as genre-blurring hits helped define the era. The collaboration reached No. 2 on the Hot 100.

“Choosin’ Texas,” meanwhile, has contributed to country’s prominence this decade .

Streaming and radio airplay at country, pop and adult formats helped sustain both hits’ extraordinary longevity. “Meant To Be” spent 55 weeks atop Country Streaming Songs, with “Choosin’ Texas” up to 44. Their commands on Country Airplay were one and three weeks, respectively (reflecting radio’s more focused programming cycles).

entertainment.title: How Jax Taylor is handling backlash over cancer diagnosis after ex Stassi Schroeder’s shady reaction

entertainment.body:
Jax Taylor is ignoring the negativity and prioritizing his well-being following his ex-girlfriend Stassi Schroeder’s shady reaction to his cancer diagnosis .

“Jax is aware of the noise online but is choosing to tune it out and focus on his health, his son and the people who have shown up for him,” a source close to the “Vanderpump Rules” alum — who shares 5-year-old Cruz with estranged wife Brittany Cartwright — told Page Six exclusively.

“Jax is fully aware that his past has given people reasons to question him,” our insider continued. “But mocking someone’s cancer diagnosis says far more about the character of those doing it than it does about him.”

Our informant noted that this coming Saturday, Nov. 28, will mark two years since Taylor, 47, got clean and sober, wondering, “At what point do people stop holding him hostage to his past and allow him the opportunity to demonstrate growth and change?”

“You don’t have to like someone to have compassion for what they’re going through,” our source argued.

The “Valley” alum — who is navigating a contentious divorce with Cartwright — has been “very intentional about who he keeps in his life” over the past year, with our insider adding that he is “recovering well and getting stronger each day” following his recent operation.

entertainment.title: Hollywood Heavyweights Urge Dems to Dump Schumer
entertainment.summary: Actors Robert De Niro, Jane Fonda, and Chelsea Handler are rallying support for Chris Van Hollen for Senate Majority Leader
entertainment.body:
A choir of celebrities and donors are urging Democrats to jettison New York Sen. Chuck Schumer from his leadership position as the party prepares to retake control of the Senate in January.

More than two dozen actors and Democratic donors signed a letter calling on members of the incoming majority to replace Schumer with his challenger , Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland, according to The New York Times .

“The Senate Democratic leader will be chosen behind closed doors, by secret ballot,” authors of the letter wrote, per the Times . “No senator will ever have to tell voters, or us, how they voted. We believe a decision this consequential deserves public accountability.”

After a long stretch in either the minority or holding the very slimmest majority in the chamber, Democrats will return to the Senate with a commanding 56-seat majority, the largest the party has had in more than 20 years.

But despite Democrats’ impressive electoral gains, the party — and Schumer in particular – remain deeply unpopular. According to a recent Economist/YouGov poll, 50 percent of Americans surveyed held a negative view of Schumer — a higher unfavorability rating than Jim Jordan, Tucker Carlson, or Stephen Miller. (Only JD Vance was viewed more negatively, with 52 percent of respondents holding unfavorable views of the vice president.)

Liberal activists are particularly sour on Schumer. Indivisible, MoveOn, the Working Families Party, and Our Revolution are among those backing Van Hollen over Schumer, who they say has been an ineffective opposition leader.

In an interview with the Times , the comedian Chelsea Handler , who signed the letter, described the 2026 election as an inflection point. “This is an opportunity. This is a window… We need to, like, get the ball and run with it. And I don’t believe that Chuck Schumer is going to do that.”

The reported signatories, who collectively gave more than $23 million for Democratic Senate and House candidates this cycle, include longtime Trump antagonist Robert De Niro , activist and actress Jane Fonda , Top Chef host Padma Lakshmi , actress Marisa Tomei , and Seinfeld and Curb Your Enthusiasm writer David Mandel. entertainment.title: Pearl Jam Slams ‘Cold Cruelty’ of ICE After ‘Unconscionable’ Detainments at Seattle Airport
entertainment.summary: "We stand firmly against this kind of inhumane treatment," the rockers wrote.
entertainment.body:
The members of Pearl Jam have joined the anti-ICE protests happening in their home city following the aggressive detainments of two people boarding a plane in Seattle over the weekend.

In a Monday (Nov. 23) post on Instagram , the band shared a photo of protestors holding signs and wrote, “It is heartbreaking and infuriating to watch the human toll of a system driven by cold cruelty.”

“Seeing a family torn apart and dragged off a jetway right here in our own airport by masked individuals is unconscionable and we stand firmly against this kind of inhumane treatment,” the caption continued. “That’s why this election mattered so much. It showed we aren’t powerless or screaming into a void. Americans stood up, looked at the systematic abuse and what ICE is doing to our neighbors, and said, no more.”

The statement comes one day after viral videos of ICE officers taking two people — a father and a daughter — into custody sparked renewed outrage over the Trump administration’s immigration enforcement policies. As Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza and Sofia Hernandez Mejia were boarding a plane at Seattle-Tacoma International Airport on their way to a family baptism ceremony in California, masked agents forcefully intercepted them and took them into custody.

When reached for comment, a spokesperson for the DHS told Billboard that it had “conducted a targeted enforcement operation to arrest Ricardo Larrondo Mendoza,” claiming that he’d “overstayed his visa in violation of our nation’s laws.”

The statement added that Mejia — whom the DHS says has also overstayed her visa — had “hurled hot coffee on the officers” and “will be charged with assaulting a federal officer.”

entertainment.title: ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ Album’s Secret Weapon? The ‘Barbie’ Soundtrack Creator
entertainment.summary: Atlantic Music Group president Kevin Weaver helped craft the video game's wide and diverse soundtrack, which features the likes of Keith Richards, Morgan Wallen, Lana Del Rey and Travis Scott.
entertainment.body:
For the biggest game the studio has ever released, Grand Theft Auto VI developer Rockstar Games wanted an equally ambitious soundtrack. Like much of the entertainment business these days, they turned to Atlantic Records to help make that happen.

Over the past decade, the record label’s soundtrack efforts, spearheaded by Atlantic Music Group President Kevin Weaver, have established Atlantic as the de-facto landing spot for media companies looking to build a star-studded accompanying album for their work. Since 2015, Atlantic has handled the soundtracks for movies including Furious 7, Suicide Squad, Greatest Showman, F1, Twisters and most-famously Barbie, the latter of which became a cultural phenomenon alongside the film itself.

But the biggest opportunity Atlantic has seen to this point wasn’t a movie, but rather a video game.

“I went to Rockstar and said that they control the most culturally relevant IP on the planet, and that what they do with music is incredible,” Weaver told The Hollywood Reporter over the phone from Miami — where he’d spent much of last week attending launch events for the game — as he recalled the initial pitch to the company. “Music is such an endemic part of the game and what GTA is. Why don’t we endeavor to do something similar to what I’d done on Barbie and these other soundtracks and A&R a whole lot of new records? ”

Weaver produced the soundtrack along with fellow Atlantic execs Joseph Khoury, Cody Verdecias, and Brandon Davis. GTA marked new territory for Weaver, the first time he’d taken on a video game soundtrack, which as he acknowledges, wasn’t on his purview before the game came into the fold.

“I’d never been interested in doing a video game soundtrack, to be honest with you,” Weaver says. “We license a lot of music to games, and I’ve had plenty of game companies come to me over the years, but if I’m not moving the needle and elevating the next thing I do, I’m not doing it. This was a natural choice, this was the one.”

Similar to the process with film soundtracks, early on, Rockstar showed Atlantic some key scenes from the game they wanted music for that were mostly set to temp tracks to help show the overall tone and feel they were looking for.

Among the first artists they reached out to, Weaver says, was Travis Scott, with some of the other earlier asks including Morgan Wallen and Dua Lipa. Scott, Weaver says, turned in the first song, with “Rhyno,” one of the soundtrack’s initial singles. Another Scott track, “Burn This Shit Down,” plays prominently during a key mission in chapter one.

entertainment.body:
Bill Maher and Byron Allen have a date with Los Angeles City College Foundation.

The pair are set for top honors at the institution’s gala — taking place at Four Seasons’ Beverly Wilshire Hotel on Dec. 2 — with Maher poised to receive the Rodney Respect Award while Allen will take home an Impact Award (presented to him by Adam Carolla ). The program, hosted by sportscaster, author and radio journalist Ted Sobel, will also shine a spotlight on Richard and Marjorie Fond, who will receive the Outstanding Alumni Award for their “professional achievements and commitment to education and philanthropy.” Related Stories Lifestyle Harrison Ford Kisses Calista Flockhart on Stage as Couple Receives Their First Joint Award TV After 2026 Midterms, Bill Maher Asks Trump, "Donnie, Are You OK?"

The Rodney Respect Award is named after late comedy icon Rodney Dangerfield. LACC is home to the Rodney Dangerfield Institute, which offers four classes including a stand-up workshop, improvisational comedy, joke writing and an American film comedy genre class. He created and hosts the long-running Comics Unleashed with Byron Allen on CBS. Allen Media Group also produces the gameshow Funny You Should Ask , also airing weeknights on CBS.

You Can See Everything was one of the biggest breakout movies of the year, racking up positive reviews , big box office numbers, and awards buzz — a rarity for a nearly three-hour documentary.

You Can See Everything , directed by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim, ups the ante on Fielder’s brand of intimate, awkward interactions. In the film, he spends over a month living with Elizabeth Holmes and her partner, Billy Evans, just before Holmes heads to prison for financial crimes related to her failed biotech company, Theranos. The documentary also marks a major year for Oppenheim, who helmed this year’s acclaimed Robert Pattinson-starring Primetime .

You Can See Everything features a surprisingly significant appearance by Amanda Seyfried, who played Holmes in the Hulu series The Dropout . The series was one of a number of films and books about Holmes , whose case became one of the most notorious financial crimes of the 21st century. Yet somehow, You Can See Everything managed to frame the story in an entirely new light, in part thanks to Seyfried’s apperance.

In an extensive interview with Rolling Stone , Seyfried discussed her eagerness to be a part of the film with Fielder and Oppenheim. “When you needed me, I came because of how invested you were, and how I felt like we were all on the same page at a point,” she said to the co-directors. “We were like a band. We were like a team. It felt like part of the team. And when I felt part of the team, it made me want to go even further. It’s not necessarily about being safe, but about doing something different.”

entertainment.title: The Rings Of Power: What Are The Silmarils, Tolkien's Legendary Jewels?
entertainment.summary: The Rings of Power has just released episodes five and six of Season 3, and the Silmarils play a big role. What exactly are these legendary jewels?
entertainment.body:

In "The Rings of Power" Season 3, Episode 6 , we get a reference to the three jewels called the Silmarils. J.R.R. Tolkien's posthumously published book "The Silmarillion" explains that this trio was made before the Two Trees of Valinor were destroyed and that they're "filled with their light." In the episode, the hallowed Silmarils come up in conversation when the dead ghost of Celebrimbor (Charles Edward) talks about the famous elven smith Fëanor crafting both the Silmarils and the Palantíri. We already know a bit about how the Palantíri work (both in "The Rings of Power" and Tolkien's source material) , but what about the Silmarils? They're important enough to have a book named after them. What are they for and what can they do?

To understand the Silmarils properly, you've got to start with their maker. Fëanor is one of the most impressive elves to ever live. "Impressive" is the key word there. He isn't a great guy, and he makes some horrible life choices, but Fëanor is ridiculously talented. He's hands-down the most skilled elven craftsman (or crafts-elf?) to ever live. He perfectly blends magic and hard skill, and his greatest feat is the creation of this trifecta of hallowed jewels. As for the motivation behind their creation, the Silmarils come about from a desire to preserve an imperishable facet of the glory of the Two Trees of Valinor.

Prime Video The Silmarils are closely connected to the Two Trees of Valinor. The pair of arboreal wonders are the sources of night and day in the immortal lands in the west of Middle-earth. They're associated with an otherworldly glory and majesty, and the Silmarils are made to contain a piece of that glory and majesty.

"The Silmarillion" says of their origin, "Then [Fëanor] began a long and secret labour, and he summoned all his lore, and his power, and his subtle skill; and at the end of all he made the Silmarils." No one knows how they were made except for their maker. Each one has an outer layer of crystal-like substance that the book says is "more strong than adamant, so that no violence could mar it or break it within the Kingdom of Arda." (Arda is Tolkien's name for the world.) But that is just their outer shell. Inside, it contains a blended inner fire sourced from the Two Trees themselves. That means the jewels glow from their own inner light. The book "Unfinished Tales" adds the fun detail that Fëanor may have gotten the idea for the Silmarils after seeing Galadriel's hair, which famously caught and reflected some of the intermingled light.

entertainment.summary: More adventures in Middle-earth are on the way: Prime Video has renewed The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power for Season 4 - see who's coming back.
entertainment.body:
"The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power" continues to be precious to Prime Video, scoring a Season 4 renewal at the streamer, TVLine has learned. This news coincides with the fantasy drama's third season finale; the final two episodes of Season 3 will be available to stream on Tuesday, November 24 at 9 pm ET.

Currently in pre-production, Season 4 will begin filming in Spring 2027 at the UK's Shepperton Studios. News of the renewal also came with a special video announcement, which you can watch above.

Showrunners J.D. Payne and Patrick McKay are also confirmed to be returning for Season 4, executive-producing alongside Lindsey Weber, Kate Hazell, Justin Doble, and director Charlotte Brändström.

"'The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power' has become a defining series for Prime Video," Peter Friedlander, Head of Global Television for Amazon MGM Studios, says in a statement. "As Season 3 delivers the landmark moment fans have been waiting for — the forging of the One Ring — we are proud to confirm Season 4 with J.D. Payne, Patrick McKay, and the entire creative team. We look forward to bringing fans even deeper into the rich world of Tolkien's Second Age."

Prime Video Season 3 of "The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power" takes place five years after Eregion's fall, with Middle-earth now at war. Sauron has been successful, managing to conquer much of the world with the help of his dark army, and his obsession with the "One Ring to rule them all" grows by the day.

So, what's a creature to do? Per Prime Video's official logline, "all the free peoples of Middle-earth — Dwarves, Elves, Men, and Wizards alike — must find a way to come together" in Season 3 "to prevent Sauron from achieving his goal of utter domination of all life."

Prime Video released the eight-episode third season over the course of three weeks, dropping the first four episodes on November 11, followed by two more pairs on November 18 and November 24.

The sprawling ensemble cast of Season 3 included Morfydd Clark as Galadriel, Charlie Vickers as Sauron, Jamie Campbell Bower as Celeborn, Ismael Cruz Córdova as Arondir, Tyroe Muhafidin as Theo, Robert Aramayo as Elrond and Elros, Owain Arthur as Durin IV, Sophia Nomvete as Disa, Benjamin Walker as Gil-galad, Daniel Weyman as Gandalf, Trystan Gravelle as Pharazôn, Maxim Baldry as Isildur, Cynthia Addai-Robinson as Míriel, Lloyd Owen as Elendil, Ciarán Hinds as the Dark Wizard, Andrew Richardson as Anárion, and Rory Kinnear as Tom Bombadil. It's not yet known how many of those actors will return for Season 4.

sports.title: Titans have only defense in the NFL giving up scores on most of its drives
sports.summary: The Titans' defense allowed the Cowboys' offense to score on every drive on Sunday, with the exception of a kneeldown at the end of the game.
sports.body:
Tennessee’s defense has now given up a score on 50.5 percent of opposing possessions this season. The Titans are the only defense in the league that gives up points most of the time it takes the field.

Over the last two games, the Titans’ defense went on an incredible run: In addition to giving up scores on the Cowboys’ first eight offensive possessions in Week 11, the Titans gave up points on the Jaguars’ last five possessions in Week 10. That streak of 13 consecutive drives giving up scores is the longest streak of consecutive drives in which any NFL defense has given up points, for as far back as full drive data is available.

The Titans’ defense’s last 14 drives ended in 10 touchdowns, three field goals and a kneeldown.

Titans coach Robert Saleh has had success as a defensive coordinator, but he went 20-36 in his previous stint as head coach of the Jets, and he’s now 1-9 with the Titans. When he’s the head coach, his defenses don’t get the job done.

Buechele has been with the Bills for most of the last four seasons, but he did have a brief stint on the Chiefs’ roster after Patrick Mahomes was injured last year. He made his regular season debut for Kansas City during that stint and went 7-of-14 for 88 yards in Week 18.

The Colts also announced that they have signed veteran defensive end Carl Lawson off of their practice squad. They placed defensive end Caden Curry on injured reserve and waived offensive tackle Charlie Heck in corresponding moves.

Wester muffed a pair of punts in the loss to the Panthers, with Carolina recovering one of them.

A sixth-round pick in last year’s draft, Wester averaged 8.2 yards per punt return and 23.7 yards per kick return in 11 games this season. He averaged 12.4 yards per punt return and 24.6 yards per kick return in 2025.

Wester also contributed five catches for 58 yards in 2026. But with four fumbles this season and three in the last three games, Baltimore has elected to move on.

Johnson was released by the Eagles earlier this month and he signed to the practice squad in Kansas City last week. He played in seven games for the Eagles this season and 58 games for the team since the start of the 2023 season.

Right tackle Jaylon Moore is dealing with an ankle injury so Johnson gives them team experienced depth up front.

VanSumeren has a knee injury. He had five special teams tackles in six games this season.

In 14 games for the Packers last year, Parsons tallied 12.5 sacks with 12 tackles for loss and 27 quarterback hits. He also had one pass defensed and two forced fumbles.

Though he wasn’t able to finish the 2025 season, he was still an AP first-team All-Pro for the third time in his career.

Green Bay had an open spot on its 53-man roster, so the club did not need to make a corresponding move.

sports.title: Bengals-Commanders clock error brings back memories of Steelers-Chargers clock error in 2015
sports.summary: Monday night's game between the Bengals and Commanders ended with an apparent error by the clock operator.
sports.body:
The Chargers were hosting the Steelers. Here’s the NFL’s official explanation , issued after the game:

“With 2:56 remaining in the fourth quarter, San Diego kicked off to Pittsburgh. The kick resulted in a touchback. By rule, the game clock does not start if the receiving team possesses the ball in the end zone and does not carry it into the field of play.

“Because of an error by the clock operator, the game clock was incorrectly started before the Steelers’ first play from scrimmage following the touchback. That first down snap came with 2:38 left to play instead of 2:56, a difference of 18 seconds.

“The official game time is kept on the stadium scoreboard, but it is the responsibility of the side judge to supervise the timing of the game. Had the side judge or any of the other six on-field officials noticed the timing error, they could have corrected it.

“The game clock is not subject to instant replay review unless there is a timing issue on the last play of the first half or the last play of the game. The performance of the clock operator and game officials will be reviewed per the standard procedure for reviewing every play of every game.”

The Steelers-Chargers situation shows that, when a clock error happens, the side judge becomes responsible for not catching it. On Monday night, that role was filled by Jimmy Buchanan. It was his job to ensure that the clock stopped when it was supposed to stop.

What comes next remains to be seen. In 2015, more than two years before the Supreme Court opened the floodgates for legalized gambling, the NFL interviewed the clock operator and side judge Rob Vernatchi .

The error in the 2015 game didn’t impact the outcome; the Steelers won the game, 24-20. Vernatchi was nevertheless suspended for a week . The NFL thereafter implemented the “ right controls ” to keep it from happening again.

sports.title: Hammond mayor says Bears will "make a lot more money" in Indiana
sports.summary: Money talks.
sports.body:
At a time when the Bears are trying to get Illinois to pass a law that will lay the foundation for a stadium in the state where the Bears have always played, Indiana interests aren’t giving up.

“The Bears are going to make more money if they come to Indiana, a lot more,” Hammond Mayor Tom McDermott Jr. recently said, via the Chicago Daily Herald . “They’ll be able to have more money every year because we have a better business environment, and if they stay in Illinois, it’s not because they got a better deal. It’s because they’re being nostalgic.”

That’s a good way to put it, if the numbers support it. To the extent that the Bears and/or the league has concerns about going to Indiana, money can alleviate such issues.

For now, it seems that the Bears are still using Indiana to get Illinois to do something. At some point, the Bears need to make a decision — one that at least 23 other owners will support.

If they wanted to go to Indiana, ground would have already been broken. At some point, however, they may have no choice but to get out the shovel. Even if getting out the shovel is the thing that will finally get Illinois to view Indiana as something more than a sham.

Five of the last seven contests are at home, with the road games coming at New England in Week 14 and, three weeks later, at the Jets.

They could win all seven. Falcons, Panthers, at Patriots, Lions, Commanders, at Jets, Bears. The toughest of the bunch will be the division games, but both will be at home. Even if they split that pair and win the rest, that’s potentially 13-4.

It won’t be easy, but it won’t be nearly as challenging as the last four games. The offense has improved and the defense (assuming the 49ers haven’t provided the rest of the league with a blueprint for beating the Brian Flores blitz) continues to be among the best in the league.

It won’t be easy, but it’s hardly impossible. One game at a time, they can resume stacking wins.

And they may inevitably cross paths with the 49ers again in January, where it would begin not at 35-10 but 0-0. Without altitude being an issue. And with a chance to have a handful of key moments that went against them in the first meeting possibly go their way in the rematch, where the pressure will be on the team that made quick and easy work of the Vikings the first time around.

sports.title: As Chargers struggle, Jim Harbaugh's answer on defensive playcalling raises more questions
sports.summary: Chargers head coach Jim Harbaugh's non-answer to a question about which defensive player is wearing the helmet with a radio receiver to tell his teammates the play call is raising more questions about whether Harbaugh has become checked out on his team.
sports.body:
Harbaugh was asked by a reporter about adjusting to different players wearing the helmet, which is designated by a green dot, and calling the defense. Harbaugh didn’t seem to know how to answer the question.

“Um, yeah, I think, uh, I’m sure there — I don’t know exactly how much of an adjustment it is,” Harbaugh said.

Asked who was wearing the green dot in Sunday’s loss to the Jets, Harbaugh didn’t know and asked if someone else could tell him before he speculated that it might have been linebackers Marlowe Wax, Del’Shawn Phillips or Troy Dye.

“Um, a few, I think, uh — who had the green dot? — I’m not for sure. Marlowe Wax, Del’Shawn. Uh, Troy might have had a green dot as well,” Harbaugh said.

Asked whether more than one player was wearing the green dot helmet at different points in the game, Harbaugh said that was his understanding.

Harbaugh played quarterback in the NFL, was an offensive coach when he was an assistant, and has generally been more involved with the offense. So perhaps he doesn’t need to know every detail of what’s going on with the defense. But the Jim Harbaugh who coached the 49ers from 2011 to 2014 was a focused, detail-oriented coach who likely would have known the answer to that question.

Harbaugh has won everywhere he’s been a head coach. At San Diego, Stanford and Michigan he had great success in college, he led the 49ers to the Super Bowl, and until this year he had a winning record with the Chargers. But now he’s 1-9, and it’s hard not to notice that he seems less involved in running his team than he used to.

sports.title: MVP race is currently down to Joe Burrow and Brock Purdy
sports.summary: With 11 weeks down and seven to go, the MVP race is currently down to two players.
sports.body:
The favorites for the top individual honor are Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow and 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy.

The next guy on the list is Bills quarterback Josh Allen, at +850. Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes is +1600.

It can, and will, change. A huge game from Allen or Mahomes (or both) on Thanksgiving night could close the gap. For now, though, it’s Burrow and Purdy.

Purdy strengthened his case on Sunday night, by cracking the code on the Minnesota defense. If the 49ers ultimately secure the No. 1 seed in the NFC, that’ll help Purdy’s case, too.

Regardless, Purdy is finally getting the appreciation he deserves. And the ultimate acknowledgement will come if he ultimately takes home the MVP award — making him the first 49ers player to win it since Steve Young in 1994.

sports.title: Jim Harbaugh on Omarion Hampton: In hindsight, we should have used him as lead back sooner

sports.body:

During a press conference on Monday, head coach Jim Harbaugh said he’s seen confidence from Hampton that’s grown in tandem with “the touches and the rhythm” of the last two weeks.

“In hindsight, we should have done that sooner,” Harbaugh said.

It’s an honest answer, but it’s not a particularly reassuring one about the job that Harbaugh and the entire Chargers coaching staff have done this year.

sports.title: Stephen Jones say the "time is nigh" to make a decision on the Bears' next stadium
sports.summary: As the Bears continue to do an awkward Bossa Nova with Indiana and Illinois over the location of a new stadium, a key executive from another team has chimed in.
sports.body:
“ The time is nigh to get something done ,” Cowboys COO and co-owner Stephen Jones told Eric Fisher of Front Office Sports . “This definitely feels like it’s coming to a head and getting to the point of a decision.”

On the surface, it seems unconventional (to say the least) for an owner of one team to speak publicly about the business affairs of another team. The fact that Jones has a seat on the league-wide body responsible for stadiums makes it somewhat less unusual.

“As a [stadium] committee member, I want the Bears to have the very best, and what is now clear is that the Bears are going to have great options, and ultimately, a special building,” Jones told Fisher. “We need the Bears to be one of the top franchises in the league. . . . It’s getting time to make a decision.”

The comments likely aren’t intended to put the squeeze on the Bears. They seem to be part of the calculated effort to get Illinois to pass legislation that would lay the foundation for a new venue that would keep the team from crossing the border to Indiana — especially with the current legislative session ending on December 3.

The problem seems to be that the powers-that-be in Illinois don’t view Indiana as a viable option for the Bears. Illinois likely sees it as a leverage play aimed at getting Illinois to do what needs to be done.

That will change only when the Bears and the NFL persuade Illinois that they’re serious about Indiana. Jones did his part in addressing the dynamics of a regional relocation across state lines.

“We’ve seen that across the league,” Jones told Fisher. “It’s hard to develop and build these buildings, but they’ve done it or are doing it now, and it’s been working out great.”

It’s one of the most basic realities of negotiations. The “or else” alternative isn’t taken seriously until it’s regarded as a viable alternative. Which can result in an ongoing game of chess morphing into a short-fused game of chicken.

sports.title: Uncalled illegal formation (if there was one) wouldn't have resulted in 10-second runoff
sports.summary: Yes, the officials missed an apparent issue with the clock last night, after the Commanders kicked a game-winning field goal.
sports.body:
That’s not to say there wasn’t an illegal formation on the play that resulted in a spike that killed the clock with four seconds to play. There likely was. Even though the X receiver was holding his hand forward to signify he intended to be on the line of scrimmage, he seemed to be behind it. Which would have given the Commanders fewer than seven men on the line.

However, illegal formation isn’t one of the fouls that trigger a 10-second runoff. So it would have resulted in a five-yard penalty and nothing more.

The issue came up in 2014 , in a Browns-Falcons game. Also, the NFL’s Approved Rulings confirm that there’s no runoff. We also confirmed the lack of a runoff with someone who knows the rules inside and out.

The reason is simple. Illegal formation doesn’t shut down a play, like a false start does.

Still, even without the runoff, the foul shouldn’t have been missed. The Commanders should have been pushed back by five yards, making the 26-yard field-goal try a 31-yard attempt.

As it was, the kick from Drew Stevens nearly hit the upright . If the ball had been struck the same way five yards farther from the target, the kick would have been no good. And the Commanders wouldn’t have walked off (when it shouldn’t have been a walk-off) with a win.

That’s the issue. Even without a runoff, a five-yard penalty may have resulted in a miss — just like it did last month for Packers kicker Trey Smack in Detroit, when a late-game kick that was good from 21 ended up being no good from 26.

sports.title: Dan Quinn: Scars from our late-game losses run deep, glad Jayden Daniels won it for us
sports.summary: "I couldn't have been more proud of Jayden at the end of the game," Quinn said after the Commanders' 22-20 win.
sports.body:
“Those scars run deep,” Quinn said. “There’s no question, failures in some. And I think those scars help.”

Quinn said he trusted Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels to have the ball in his hands at the end, and wanted to manage the clock in such a way that Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow would not be the quarterback with the chance to win it at the end.

“I didn’t want [Daniels] to not touch the ball at the end of the game,” Quinn said. “This is not a quarterback on the other side that you want to have holding it at the end of the game.”

Daniels has been harshly criticized this season for mismanaging late-game situations, but Daniels made two tremendous throws on the final drive to get the Commanders into range for their game-winning field goal.

“I couldn’t have been more proud of Jayden at the end of the game,” Quinn said. “To see those guys come through at the end, I thought that was one of our best team wins. I didn’t think anything could top last week’s but tonight did.”

The Commanders are now 4-5-1 and still alive in the NFC East race. And they have some confidence that if they need their quarterback to deliver in the clutch, he’ll deliver.

sports.title: Clock operator robbed Bengals of one final play
sports.summary: The Bengals-Commanders game carries a small but not insignificant asterisk.
sports.body:
As ESPN rules analyst Russell Yurk explained in the postgame show, the clock operator incorrectly ran the remaining four seconds off the clock during the game-winning field goal from Washington.

Yurk said two seconds remained when the ball hit the net. It looks more like it should have been one second.

Regardless, Yurk said the replay process can’t restore time when the next play isn’t a scrimmage play. (There’s also a rule regarding restoring time when there are fewer than two seconds left, and — with all due respect to Yurk — it appears that there was only one second when the ball hit the net.)

The bottom line is that the clock operator was slow to get to the button, and there wasn’t anything that could be done about it.

What would have happened if the Bengals had gotten one last chance? We’ll never know, because the person hired to keep track of the time handled it incorrectly.

Or, depending on that person’s rooting interests, he handled it perfectly.

sports.title: Tee Higgins touchdown highlights inconsistency of replay review
sports.summary: Just when we thought we were out when it comes to not knowing what a catch is, they pull us back in.
sports.body:
The past two days have included three examples of plays that make more confusing the question of whether a player has completed the act of catching the ball — and whether replay review was properly used to correct rulings made on the field.

It started on Sunday afternoon, when an apparent touchdown catch by Jaguars receiver Parker Washington was ruled not a catch on the field, with replay review not overturning the ruling. Even though the visual evidence seemed to provide clear and obvious proof that the ball was caught.

On Sunday night, 49ers receiver Mike Evans bobbled his way to a touchdown catch . He quite possibly didn’t get two feet in bounds after finally securing control of the ball. The play wasn’t even reviewed.

On Monday night, Bengals receiver Tee Higgins made a touchdown catch even though the ball was moving as he landed on the ground and out of bounds. There was no replay review.

The common denominator in these plays (beyond the fact that they involved potential touchdown catches) is the shadowy, uncertain replay process. As one head coach explained it to PFT on Monday (before the Bengals-Commanders game), it’s still not known who is making the decisions in New York as to what will be reviewed and what the outcome of the review will be.

It’s another reason for the NFL to embrace full transparency when it comes to replay review. We need to know who is making the decisions. We need to know their names. We need to hear their voices.

And we also need to know why — as happened in the case of the Evans and Higgins touchdowns — there was no full-blown review.

sports.title: Mike McCarthy: Aaron Rodgers is our quarterback
sports.summary: Before an NFL team benches its starting quarterback, someone asks the coach whether the quarterback could be benched.
sports.body:
That happened for the first time during Aaron Rodgers’s two-year tenure with the team on Monday, during a press conference with coach Mike McCarthy, one day after the team’s latest loss, to the Eagles.

It came up as innocuously as possible. McCarthy wasn’t asked whether Rodgers could get the hook; McCarthy was asked whether he’s considering using one of the other three quarterbacks on the roster in an effort to mix things up when the offense is struggling.

Of course he is. Even if Rodgers’s play merits benching, Aaron Rodgers isn’t getting benched. It’s implicit in the arrangement.

Still, Aaron Rodgers is a far cry from what he once was. In 10 games this season, Rodgers has completed 220 of 361 passes for 2,241 yards, with 16 touchdown passes and six interceptions. His passer rating of 86.6 is the lowest of his career since becoming Green Bay’s starter in 2008, with the exception of a four-snap performance in 2023 with the Jets (39.6, based on one incomplete pass thrown).

At 6-4, the Steelers remain in contention for another one-and-out playoff appearance. That makes it easier to justify staying the course. With upcoming games against the Broncos, Texans, and Jaguars, that could change.

Even then, Rodgers would never be benched. He’d be “injured.” And his career would end not with a bang but with a whimper.

sports.body: I think part of being a diehard NFL fan is trying to derive meaning out of everything that happens to a team, no matter how small. Think about the offseason program. How often do we have reports on which players are up and which players are down? These continue into training camp. Then the second half of preseason games produce deep dive analysis of which players are potentially hidden gems or important depth pieces. Every now and then an OTA, training camp, or preseason, breakout turns out to be a preview of a genuine step forward by a developing player. Far more often the players and the hype are forgotten. It also goes this way in late season games when a team has fallen out of the Playoff race. Can a loss help a team secure a high Draft pick to land a franchise changing player? Can a late season surge lead to momentum carrying into a future season and be the first step in instilling a new culture? In both cases the answer is yes. Far more often, however, these games don’t have a ton of meaning either way in the long run. They amount to a bad team playing out the string. The Jets’ Week 11 victory over the Chargers has evoked passions across the fanbase. Some fans are furious about the team hurting its NFL Draft positioning. Others are happy to get the win. I don’t think there’s a “right” or a “wrong” way to be a fan. Everybody wants the same thing in the end, for the Jets to have success. Opinions simply vary on the best way to get there. I can understand fans who are hoping for as high of a pick as possible. Of course, we have seen over and over that the quality of the coaching staff and front office making the pick are generally far more important than where the pick is made. Earlier this season, I published two corresponding studies that examined how scoring right before the end of the half and “double-dipping” correlate to winning. I used a dataset that features all regular-season games from 2001 to 2025 and, at time of publication, the first three weeks of the 2026 season. sports.body: The Buffalo Bills beat the Dolphinss 26-9 in Week 11 at Highmark Stadium, in a game that was far from perfection from Joe Brady’s but felt more impressive than last week’s win over the Jets. The Bills are now 9-1. These are my takeaways from Buffalo’s victory. Josh Allen came out ready to let it rip And I loved it. Not necessarily because Allen always made the “right” decision determining at which level to throw the football. I want defenses to be forced to think about all possible variations of Buffalo’s offense. And Allen is the best player in football. The Bills slammed their foot on the gas pedal to begin this game, and while it didn’t amount to something like three-consecutive touchdown drives — which we’ve certainly witnessed during the Allen era — it led to three pass plays of 20-plus yards and two touchdowns in the first half as Buffalo built its lead. Allen seemed adamant about dicing the Dolphins secondary through the air, and not underneath. That is Allen being Allen. Allen didn’t have a carry against the Dolphins, which now amounts to, ironically, a similar place to where we were after the Patriots loss, when the Allen criticism centered around him throwing it downfield too frequently and not running nearly enough. And what happened after that? Allen averaged 11.1 yards per attempt and ran for 121 yards on 10 carries in a 37-34 win on the road against the Rams. The safety group has become a strength Amazing, right? Even if you don’t fully agree with me, it’s impossible it ignore the difference in the play of this group recently compared to the first month or so of the season. Cole Bishop is so perfectly positioned in his box/blitz role that asks him to cover the slot underneath. He’s become a weapon as an addition to the pass rush, and his size plus explosiveness and strength allow the Bills to defend the run respectably in dime, if needed. Good early returns on Amani Hooker, as he’s allowed four catches for 47 yards with two pass breakups, nine total tackles, and a quarterback hit on three pass-rush snaps in his two contests with the Bills. And, heck, new safety No. 3, Damar Hamlin, had the biggest splash play of the group against Miami, an impressive interception at the intermediate level. Jordan Hancock played outstandingly in the safety/slot hybrid role, and the Bills even got Jalon Kilgore and Sam Franklin Jr. onto the field in this contest.

sports.title: Buffalo Bills RB James Cook III makes NFL history in Week 11
sports.summary: Buffalo Bills running back James Cook III has spent much of the 2026 season putting together one of the most consistent stretches of rushing production in NFL history. With another strong performance against the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, Cook now has a place on the all-time leaderboard all to himsel
sports.body: Buffalo Bills running back James Cook III has spent much of the 2026 season putting together one of the most consistent stretches of rushing production in NFL history. With another strong performance against the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, Cook now has a place on the all-time leaderboard all to himself. With Sunday’s performance, which included 89 rushing yards and a touchdown, Cook became just the second player in NFL history to rush for at least 75 yards and score a rushing touchdown in nine consecutive games, moving past three former NFL running backs who had each reached eight straight. Notably, he’s the only player in league history to put up those numbers in one season. [Media: https://twitter.com/BuffaloBillsPR/status/2124605029529403539?a=SI4XCAzJ3357jRKxHXM&s=20] Cook entered the game tied with Pro Football Hall of Famers John Riggins and LaDainian Tomlinson, along with George Rogers, for the second-longest streak in NFL history. Riggins accomplished the feat in 1983, Rogers did it across the 1985 and 1986 seasons, and Tomlinson matched them in 2006. The 27-year-old Cook joined that group during Buffalo’s Week 10 victory over the New York Jets. He rushed for 157 yards on 18 carries, including a career-long 74-yard touchdown run in the second half of the Bills’ 31-12 win. Now, only Terry Allen stands ahead of Cook. Allen reached 10 consecutive games with at least 75 rushing yards and a touchdown while playing for Washington across the 1995 and 1996 seasons. With nine straight games behind him, Cook is now within striking distance of a record that’s stood for 30 years, but the road won’t get any easier. Kansas City and New England are next on Buffalo’s schedule, and the dates next to those names are just as challenging as the opponents. The Bills have just three days to rest, recover, and prepare to host the Chiefs on Thanksgiving night. If Cook is going to catch Terry Allen, he’ll have to keep his streak alive through one of the toughest stretches of Buffalo’s season.

sports.body: Buffalo Bills outside linebacker Greg Rousseau has reinvented himself this year. A new position, a new number, new coaches and an entirely new defensive scheme. And the results? Is it too early to start throwing around the word legendary? Maybe, but Rousseau is certainly making a case for it. With two sacks against the Miami Dolphins on Sunday, Rousseau has officially entered uncharted territory in his NFL career. His 10 sacks this season are a new personal best. [Media: https://twitter.com/BuffaloBillsPR/status/2124568810426356152?a=PKP5mAXAD9DcankXAG0&s=20] Rousseau sacked Miami quarterback Kyle McCord for an eight-yard loss that forced the Dolphins to punt after a five-play first drive. Then in the second quarter, it was an almost identical play. Rousseau dropped McCord for another eight-yard loss. [Media: https://twitter.com/BuffaloBillsPR/status/2124585141821452485?a=LnRiXda6MHK5TN5rwfs&s=20] Rousseau entered the NFL in 2021 as a defensive end, spending his first five seasons in Sean McDermott’s defensive system. Along the way, he worked under Leslie Frazier, McDermott himself, and Bobby Babich as defensive leaders, while learning from defensive line coaches Eric Washington and Marcus West. Then came 2026, and just about everything changed. Jim Leonhard took over as defensive coordinator, bringing a new scheme that moved Rousseau from defensive end to outside linebacker. Bobby April III became his new position coach, giving Rousseau his third position coach and fourth defensive leader in six NFL seasons. Somehow, through all that change, Rousseau is putting together the most productive season of his career. He recorded four sacks as a rookie in 2021, eight in 2022, five in 2023, eight again in 2024 and seven last season. Those eight-sack performances had been his personal best until Sunday. sports.body: It’s a beautiful victory, Monday, New York Jets fans! I’m sure everyone is happy about this dub, right? Wrong. The fan base is fractured down the middle with this result. Some fans are happy to see their team win for the first time in five weeks. While others are pulling their hair out over what they describe as a frustrating loss to a crappy opponent that screwed up their draft positioning. “A Jets win that feels like a loss to many people in the fan base, and I don’t blame anyone who feels that way because I feel the same way. Watching the Jets go out there and win this game just leaves that sinking feeling in your stomach oh my God they have ruined the tank again. That’s the feeling many in the fan base have, and if you feel that way, you’re not a bad fan because you see the forest through the trees because you understand that a win over a one-win Chargers team could potentially do more damage than good. If you’re going to win games, you want it to be because your young players are playing great, not because 33-year-old Sterling Shepard is scoring two touchdowns on his only two touches of the game,” ESPN New York’s Jake Asman lamented. The Jets were not going to finish 2-15. Anyone who set that expectation set themselves up for failure. They have been in a ton of close games this season. A broken clock is right twice a day. A blind squirrel can find a nut. The Jets were eventually going to stumble into a victory, and who knows if this is the last one. There are still six games left in the 2026 regular season. For fans who like seeing their green and white team win regardless of circumstance, cheers to you today. We’ve only had three wins this year; enjoy them while you can. --- J-E-T-S! sports.body: The New York Jets broke a five game losing streak and got their third win of the season on Sunday against the Los Angeles Chargers. The Jets are now 3-8 on the season, in third place in the AFC East. The Jets scored on the opening drive of the game and never looked back. The Jets never trailed in the game. They scored every time they had the ball other than their last possession, when they ran out the clock to seal the win. The Jets offense bullied the Chargers defense all day. The running game was efficient and effective. The Jets converted on better than 80% of their third downs. Geno Smith was accurate and efficient, spreading the ball around effectively. Practice squad call-up Sterling Shepard scored twice. It was a really nice offensive performance by the Jets. Defensively the Jets struggled, but David Bailey got another two sacks to get to 9.5 for the season and the offense was good enough to get the victory. The win over the Chargers left the Jets with a 3-8 record to start the season, in 3rd place in the AFC East. Though mathematical elimination is still probably a month or so away, it has become obvious the Jets playoff drought will extend to 16 years and counting by season’s end. The Jets are also just one loss away from their 11th straight losing season. Now the Jets go on the road to face the 1-9 Miami Dolphins. The Dolphins’ only win this season came at the expense of the Jets a few weeks ago. Since the Dolphins’ victory over the Jets in October the Dolphins lost three straight competitive games to the New England Patriots, Detroit Lions and Indianapolis Colts before getting blown out this Sunday by the Buffalo Bills. Let’s take a look at the current odds for this game according to FanDuel Sportsbook. The oddsmakers think the Jets will beat the Dolphins next Sunday. The current line has the Jets road favorites by 3.5 points. The game has an over/under of 41.5 points. On the moneyline the Jets are -215 while the Dolphins are +180. A win against the Dolphins next Sunday would send the Jets going into their Week 13 bye with some momentum and a chance to finish the season on the upswing.
